original_question: Let Gamma = <g1, ..., ge> be a numerical semigroup and let p be a pseudo-Frobenius number of Gamma. An RF-matrix of p is an e x e matrix (a_ij) with a_ii = -1, a_ij in N for i != j, and sum_j a_ij g_j = p for every row i; subtracting two rows gives a relation in ker(phi), called an RF-relation. Are all minimal relations of a numerical semigroup RF-relations?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 26 ([HW19], Question 3.6): "Are all minimal relations of a numerical semigroup RF-relations?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It identifies the correct objects—numerical semigroup, pseudo-Frobenius number, RF-matrix, and RF-relation—and asks the same global question as the paper: whether every minimal relation comes from the RF-matrix construction. It also keeps the scope appropriately narrow and does not broaden the problem beyond what the paper states.
missing_details: The paper’s ambient notation is the factorization homomorphism phi: N^e -> Gamma, phi(u_1,...,u_e) = sum_i u_i g_i; relations are elements of the kernel congruence ker(phi).

A 'minimal relation' should be stated precisely as an element of a minimal generating set of ker(phi), i.e. a relation in a minimal presentation of Gamma, not merely any integer dependence among g_1,...,g_e.

To formalize the RF-relation construction, one should say that if r and s are two rows of an RF-matrix, then r - s is written as alpha - beta with alpha, beta in N^e, yielding (alpha, beta) in ker(phi).

The quantifier over pseudo-Frobenius numbers should be explicit: the question is whether each minimal relation arises from some RF-matrix attached to some p in PF(Gamma), not necessarily from a fixed p.
For full stand-alone clarity, N should be declared to be the nonnegative integers, and Gamma = <g_1,...,g_e> should be said to be minimally generated, so that e is the embedding dimension.
No field, grading, homogeneity, degree restriction, characteristic assumption, or nilpotency condition is part of this problem as stated in the paper; it is purely semigroup-theoretic.
refined_question: Let Gamma = <g_1,...,g_e> be a numerical semigroup minimally generated by g_1,...,g_e, where N denotes the nonnegative integers, and let phi: N^e -> Gamma be the factorization homomorphism phi(u_1,...,u_e) = sum_{i=1}^e u_i g_i. Let PF(Gamma) be the set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers of Gamma. For p in PF(Gamma), an RF-matrix of p is an e x e matrix A = (a_ij) such that a_ii = -1, a_ij is in N for i != j, and sum_{j=1}^e a_ij g_j = p for every row i. If r and s are two rows of A, write r - s = alpha - beta with alpha, beta in N^e; then (alpha, beta) is in ker(phi), and such a relation is called an RF-relation. Is every element of a minimal generating set of the congruence ker(phi) — equivalently, every relation in a minimal presentation of Gamma — an RF-relation arising from some RF-matrix of some p in PF(Gamma)?
justification: The draft clearly targets the paper’s Section 6 problem on RF-relations, not a neighboring result: the paragraph immediately before Problem 26 defines RF-matrices and RF-relations, and Problem 26 then asks essentially the same question as your draft. The only substantial gaps are the standing notation from Section 1—especially phi and the precise meaning of a minimal relation as a generator of ker(phi). The refined version therefore keeps exactly the scope of Problem 26 and only makes the hidden definitions explicit so that the question is fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper.
